items.cite: Carol A. Hess, *Sacred Passions: The Life and Music of Manuel de Falla* (Oxford University Press, 2005).
items.note: A biography that draws on the Granada archive to relate Falla’s life, faith and music, and sets his work in its historical and cultural context.

items.cite: Carol A. Hess, *Manuel de Falla and Modernism in Spain, 1898–1936* (University of Chicago Press, 2001).
items.note: Hess approaches Spanish modernism, and Falla’s place in the political and cultural arguments before the Civil War, through Falla’s career.

items.cite: Manuel de Falla, *On Music and Musicians* (Marion Boyars, 1979), first published in Spanish as *Escritos sobre música y músicos* (1950).
items.note: Falla’s collected essays in English translation, including his writings on the composers and traditions he admired.

items.cite: Archivo Manuel de Falla, Granada: chronology and life-and-work pages.
items.note: Dates and places of each work, journey and première, year by year, with extracts from the letters preserved in the Granada archive.

items.cite: Jaime Pahissa, *Vida y obra de Manuel de Falla* (Ricordi Americana, 1947; second edition 1956).
items.note: Pahissa, a Catalan composer in exile in Buenos Aires, made notes on what Falla said about his own life in his last years during a visit to Los Espinillos in 1944, for this early life.
